issuers.sector: Polymer compounds for wires, cables and pipe coating
issuers.headline: A profitable, cash-generative polymer compounder doubling capacity, priced at 34.5x FY26 earnings after the issue against a 14.5x peer median; our fair value is Rs 81 (Neutral) against Rs 150, because growth in the core manufactured business has been flat and the price already pays for the expansion.
red_flags: Operating EBITDA margin 5.5% -> 9.7% -> 12.0% FY24-26 (14.5% in Q1 FY27); PAT Rs 7.52 cr -> Rs 27.01 cr; cumulative CFO 118% of PAT (pp. 85-86)
Capacity to rise from 35,251 to 87,301 MTPA (+148%) by FY28 from Rs 77.56 cr of proceeds; current utilisation 73-75% (pp. 123-124)
Manufactured revenue flat to lower (Rs 254 cr -> Rs 237 cr FY24-26); growth came from resin trading, 31.9% of FY26 revenue (pp. 33, 406, 408)
Top customer 31.7% of FY26 revenue; top supplier 71.7% of procurement; purchases from promoter-group trader Vinsul Makardi 9.3% of revenue (pp. 27, 39, 89)
At Rs 150: P/E 34.5x post-issue vs peer median 14.5x (DDev Plastiks 13.0x, Kingfa 46.3x); reported P/E is a fair measure (earnings-quality adjustments -2.8%)
Fair value Rs 68 / 81 / 96 (Bear / Neutral / Bull) vs Rs 150; objects floor Rs 98; issuer KPI EBITDA leaves other income in (Rs 46.60 cr vs Rs 41.90 cr operating)

issuers.sector: Defence electronics: electro-optic and thermal imaging systems
issuers.brlm: JM Financial Limited; IIFL Capital Services Limited
issuers.headline: A leading Indian thermal-imaging OEM that owns its technology, priced at 78.8x FY26 earnings against an 85.6x peer median; our Neutral fair value is Rs 515 (-26% vs Rs 700) because FY26 was a down year with cash tied up in orders, and the outcome turns on how quickly the Rs 432 cr of orders convert.
red_flags: Owns 100% of its IP; largest supplier of thermal imaging to Indian government agencies Apr-24 to Mar-26 (issuer-paid F&S report, pp. 246, 253)
EBITDA margin 26.2% / 29.7% / 28.9% FY24-26 and cash tax 23.3% of PBT (pp. 89, 144)
Orders of Rs 432 cr in hand (Rs 314 cr book at Jun-26 plus Rs 118 cr won Jul-Sep), about 1.2x FY26 revenue (p. 250)

FY26 revenue -22.7% as export orders slipped; reported P/E 78.8x is flattered by a Rs 18.84 cr warranty write-back and Rs 34.17 cr of capitalised development (adjusted FY26 P/E 247.5x; three-year average 75.6x) (pp. 23, 351, 373)
Priced at 78.8x FY26 EPS and 7.2x book vs peer medians 85.6x and 13.0x (pp. 141, our computation)
Fair value Rs 486 / 515 / 556 (Bear / Neutral / Bull) vs Rs 700; QIB book 293.6x at close (NSE)

issuers.sector: Consumer electronics and appliances ODM/OEM (LED televisions, washing machines, coolers, speakers, cooktops)
issuers.brlm: Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors; Shannon Advisors
issuers.headline: Revenue reached Rs 1,221.8 cr in FY26 (pro-forma Rs 1,263.1 cr, +78%) at a 9.4% EBITDA margin and 18.0% ROCE, but operating cash flow has been negative in each of the three years (Rs -108.1 cr in total) and net debt is 2.6x EBITDA; the peer-multiple and cash-flow methods give values far apart, so the price band and H1 FY27 decide the case.
red_flags: Revenue Rs 0.07 cr, Rs 496.5 cr, Rs 1,221.8 cr (FY24-26); pro-forma FY26 Rs 1,263.1 cr, +78.1%; EBITDA margin 9.37%, ROCE 18.0% (pp. 74, 137)
Operating cash flow Rs -15.3 cr, -64.1 cr, -28.7 cr in FY24-26 against cumulative PAT of Rs 84.9 cr; receivables up Rs 97.3 cr and inventory Rs 38.9 cr in FY26 (p. 75)
Top 5 customers 52.4% and top 10 65.8% of FY26 revenue; top supplier 46.9% of purchases; imports 76.2% of raw materials (pp. 23, 29, 41)
FY25's largest customer (21.0% of revenue, Rs 104.3 cr) was the promoter-owned Ekkaa Electronics Industries, acquired on 29-Aug-2025; its sales were still 6.2% of FY26 revenue (pp. 78-80, 274)
Rs 525 cr fresh issue: Rs 225 cr repays loans and Rs 150 cr funds working capital; the Rs 200 cr offer for sale pays two promoters (WACA Rs 19.87 and Rs 17.53) (pp. 1, 119-120)
Net debt Rs 296.0 cr (2.58x EBITDA); borrowings Rs 396.1 cr by 31-Jul-2026 against Rs 308.8 cr at 31-Mar-2026; 19.9% industry growth to FY30 is an issuer-commissioned estimate (pp. 73, 42, 245)

issuers.sector: Agricultural implements (Super Seeders, straw reapers, rotavators, laser levellers, biomass machines)
issuers.headline: Proforma revenue grew 63% in FY26 to Rs 414.0 cr with an EBITDA margin of 13.5%, but the business only combined on 1-Apr-2025, one customer is 25% of revenue and FY26 operating cash flow was 8.6% of PAT as stock built up; at the Rs 155.78 peer-median reference the price asks for a continuation of that growth.
red_flags: Proforma revenue Rs 253.8 cr to Rs 414.0 cr (+63.1%); EBITDA Rs 36.8 cr to Rs 55.7 cr; PAT Rs 20.7 cr to Rs 31.4 cr (pp. 92, 158)
Promoters' two proprietorships were taken over on 1-Apr-2025 at carrying value; restated FY25 (Rs 95.9 cr) is not comparable with FY26 (pp. 247, 387)
Seth Agro Industries is 25.21% of FY26 revenue; top 10 customers 50.04%; top supplier only 7.94% (pp. 261, 39)
FY26 CFO Rs 2.7 cr vs PAT Rs 31.4 cr; finished goods Rs 43.2 cr vs Rs 1.9 cr; cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (pp. 88, 474)
Rs 300 cr fresh issue: 66.7% identified (Rs 110 cr working capital, Rs 71.7 cr capex on promoter-leased land, Rs 18.5 cr debt); no capex order placed (pp. 124, 129)
Net debt Rs 119.4 cr (2.14x EBITDA); borrowings Rs 164.1 cr by 31-Aug-2026; subsidy-linked demand and Q4 seasonality (pp. 56, 34)

issuers.sector: HVAC components (brass and copper tubes and fittings for air-conditioner indoor and outdoor units, refrigeration lines)
issuers.headline: PAT grew from Rs 76.70 m to Rs 332.06 m over FY24-FY26 at a 28.39% ROCE, but FY26 revenue growth slowed to 9.0% and operating cash flow was Rs -430.08 m as inventory rose to 116 days, so the RHP's H1 FY27 cash flow and the price band decide the case.
red_flags: PAT Rs 76.70 m / 271.37 m / 332.06 m FY24-FY26; ROCE 28.39% and ROE 42.86% in FY26; cash tax 25.4% of cumulative PBT (pp. 86, 182)
Supplies eight of the top ten Indian HVAC makers; 96.91% of FY26 revenue from repeat customers; installed capacity up 50% in two years (pp. 174-175, 182)
Operating cash flow Rs +37.40 / -66.47 / -430.08 m against PAT; FY26 inventory days 116 vs 50 and borrowings Rs 1,532.11 m vs 658.75 m (pp. 87, 167)
Top-10 customers 89.71% of revenue (Amber 28.79%); Supplier 1 is 32.99% of expenses; no long-term supply contracts (pp. 24-26, 430)
Customs show-cause notice Rs 130.38 m (14.2% of net worth) at the Supreme Court; Rs 74.96 m FX loss on unhedged imports in FY26 (pp. 444, 461)
Rs 1,530.00 m of new units with no plant orders placed; peer P/Es run 19.08x to 141x, so the multiple method and the DCF are far apart (pp. 133-134, 179)

issuers.headline: Revenue doubled and PAT rose 6.3x over FY24-FY26 with cash tax fully paid, but operating cash flow was negative each year as inventory grew; at the Rs 147.33 pre-IPO reference the P/E (15.6x) is in line with peers.
red_flags: Revenue CAGR 41.9% and PAT CAGR 151.7% (FY24-FY26); cash tax 26.9% of PBT
Operating cash flow negative each year; cumulative CFO/PAT -87.5%
Volume sold +1.7% while revenue per kg +97.9%: growth price-led
Top-10 customers 22.32% of revenue; top-5 suppliers 56.98% of COGS
Post-issue P/E ~15.6x at reference vs peer median 15.72x
Related party Aalishaan: 5.06% of FY26 sales; subsidiary from Apr-26

issuers.headline: Revenue rose 2.5x over FY24-FY26 to Rs 106.76 cr with PAT of Rs 13.38 cr, but operating cash flow was negative in two of three years, 83.6% of revenue comes from ten customers, and the Rs 155.03 cr of identified objects imply a price of at least Rs 44.29 against Rs 17.50 in the last secondary transfers.
red_flags: Revenue Rs 41.87 cr to Rs 106.76 cr FY24-FY26 (2.5x); PAT Rs 8.63 cr to Rs 13.38 cr, down 17.1% in FY26 (p. 84)
Cumulative CFO/PAT -25.7%; receivables 211 closing days, Rs 14.10 cr outstanding 1-3 years (pp. 39, 86-87; Annex. 14)
Top-10 customers 83.58% of FY26 revenue, top-1 18.73%; Government share fell from 58.36% to 26.84% (pp. 49-50)
Related-party purchases and services Rs 14.11 cr (24.3% of purchases); related-party supplier advances Rs 8.06 cr (pp. 89-92)
Objects floor Rs 44.29 per share vs Rs 17.50 secondary price; blended fair value Rs 17.71 (Neutral)
Contracted growth: 20-year UP concession for 20 institutes and MoU for 50 AICTE labs; 30 labs already equipped (pp. 134-145)

issuers.sector: PET recycling (recycled polyester fibre, food-grade rPET resin, chemically recycled resin)
issuers.headline: Revenue grew at a 25.3% CAGR over FY24-FY26 with positive operating cash flow each year, but PAT was flat (Rs 211.3 m to Rs 224.9 m) and ROCE stayed near 10%; the Rs 90.10 reference price is about 69x FY26 EPS, in line with the single listed peer.
red_flags: Revenue CAGR 25.3% FY24-26; PAT flat at Rs 211.3 m / 205.7 m / 224.9 m (p. 72)
Operating cash flow positive every year; cumulative CFO/PAT 201%, about 108% after interest (p. 73)
ROCE 10.28% and EBITDA margin 10.86% FY26; net debt / EBITDA 3.40x, down from 5.25x (p. 122)
Capacity utilisation 70% in FY26 on 141,000 MTPA; 180,360 MTPA at Aug-2026 (pp. 24, 225)
Revaluation reserve Rs 614.81 m = 22.5% of total equity; issuer net worth excludes it (p. 397)
Customer and supplier concentration not disclosed; audit trail not enabled at database level (pp. 43-45, 244)

issuers.brlm: IIFL Capital Services Limited; JM Financial Limited; Nuvama Wealth Management Limited
issuers.headline: India's dominant SBR sewage-treatment technology supplier (639 plants, 29.7% operating margin, net cash), moving into biogas and water reuse; our fair value is Rs 330 (Neutral), about 21x FY25 EPS, because rising working capital has kept cash conversion at about 22% of profit. Screen only until the RHP: Subscribe up to about Rs 367, Neutral to about Rs 472.
red_flags: Revenue Rs 519.45 cr -> Rs 697.86 cr FY23-25 (15.9% CAGR, +6.1% in FY25); operating EBITDA margin 23.9% -> 29.7%; ROCE about 29% (pp. 170, 364)
Working capital 27.8% -> 63.5% of revenue; receivable days 158 -> 262; cumulative CFO about 22% of PAT FY23-25 (pp. 34, 368)
Order book Rs 1,267.50 cr at 15-Aug-2025 (1.8x FY25 revenue) after Rs 501.70 cr of CBG plant orders; WWT order book down 30% in FY25 (pp. 49, 262)
Offer mostly OFS (1.23 crore shares; average cost Rs 36.72); last private price Rs 75 bonus-adjusted (Apr-2024) (pp. 45, 173)
Goa SPCB show-cause notice and FIR against subsidiary HWTPL over effluent; EUR 5.60 m claim against SFC Umwelttechnik GmbH in Portugal (pp. 507-508; corrigendum)
Fair value Rs 304 / 330 / 358 (Bear / Neutral / Bull); reported P/E a fair measure (adjustments -5.2%); audited data 570 days old
